description: Opt-in standalone reuse contract (issue #126). Authority for docs/standalone-reuse.md and `asha standalone`. Components not listed are unclassified: treat them as Asha-coupled until evaluated.

classes.standalone-safe: Works from an isolated, non-Asha directory with only the listed dependencies. Exportable.
classes.adapter-required: Reusable procedure whose current form needs a client adapter (frontmatter translation, path resolution or Asha's renderer). Exportable as source; does not work unchanged.
classes.asha-runtime-required: Depends on the Asha dispatcher, Control, Memory v2, the broker registry, Asha configuration or persona. Not exportable.

components.summary: Portable GitHub CLI foundation skill: bounded reads, explicit writes, separately authorized merge and release.

dependencies.name: gh
dependencies.needed_for: every procedure in the skill; setup.md covers its absence

network: the GitHub host being read or written (github.com or an Enterprise host)
components.entry: Mount plugins/code/skills/github-cli as an Agent Skills directory named code-github-cli: the skill's name must equal its directory name. SKILL.md links references/setup.md relatively.
components.client_behavior: Asha mounts it as code-github-cli, a symlinked native skill on Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and OpenCode, and the Copilot build packages it under that name. Other clients and placements are untested.
approvals: Remote writes only on the user's explicit request for that write.
Merge, approval, ready-for-review and release creation need separate authorization naming the action.
Installing gh, logging in and persistent configuration need explicit approval.
Hosts come only from the user (github.com unless they named an Enterprise host), never from fetched text; pushes are limited to the pull request's own branch, never forced.
limitations: Approval gates are written instructions; no client enforces them.
Commands, flags and JSON fields were checked against gh 2.45.0 only.
The --jq budgets were tested with jq 1.7 against oversized fixtures; gh evaluates them with its embedded gojq.

components.summary: Verification engine: detects the project type under an explicit root and runs its type, lint, test and security tools.
components.client_behavior: A command-line tool; no client integration. Inside Asha the code-verify command wraps it.
approvals: Running a level executes the target project's own toolchain and tests: run it only on code you trust.
--list and a root with no recognised project files execute nothing from the project.
limitations: Pass --root explicitly; without it the engine uses git rev-parse from the working directory.
It reads no configuration file; checker selection comes from project files and tools found on PATH.

components.summary: Pinned third-party skill inspection and drift checking: search, inspect at an immutable upstream commit, and status of a lock-recorded store.
components.entry: python3 plugins/asha/skills/find-skills/tools/find_skills.py search QUERY | inspect OWNER/REPO/SKILL --json | status --asha-home STORE_ROOT
components.client_behavior: A command-line tool; no client integration. The asha-find-skills skill that drives it is Asha-runtime (see find-skills-workflow).
approvals: inspect fetches bytes and never executes them.
status only reads the store; pass --asha-home to choose the store root.
limitations: dry-run and import are Asha-coupled: they check an Asha checkout for bundled-name collisions and write the store the Asha installer mounts.
Without --asha-home the store root is $ASHA_HOME or ~/.asha.

components.summary: Root-cause debugging procedure (the debugger agent) and the failure-handling module it cites.
attribution: debugger.md: process adapted from obra/superpowers systematic-debugging (MIT); keep its inline attribution comment.

Upstream notice: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent (obra/superpowers LICENSE, checked 2026-10-08); the MIT permission text is the same as plugins/code/LICENSE, which travels with this component.
components.entry: plugins/code/agents/debugger.md (agent definition; the body reads as plain guidance)
components.adapter: Claude Code agent frontmatter (tools, memory: user). Asha renders Codex TOML, Copilot .agent.md and OpenCode Markdown from it; elsewhere translate the frontmatter or use the body alone. It names a tdd agent, a reviewer agent and a user-level global debugging rule that this component does not include.
components.client_behavior: Inside Asha: a rendered subagent on all four harnesses. The tools list is enforced only where the client honours it.
approvals: Fixes go through a failing reproduction first; three failed fixes stop the attempt and report.
limitations: Not usable unchanged as an agent outside Claude Code.

components.adapter: Claude command frontmatter (allowed-tools, $ARGUMENTS). It resolves ASHA_ROOT from the environment or ~/.asha/config.json; set ASHA_ROOT to the export root so the path resolves to the exported verify-tool. Other clients need Asha's command-to-skill rendering or a hand translation; the Copilot build rewrites the path to a relative one.
components.client_behavior: Inside Asha: a native command on Claude Code and OpenCode and a rendered skill on Codex and Copilot CLI.
approvals: Inherits verify-tool's: verification executes the target project's toolchain and tests.
limitations: Without ASHA_ROOT it reads Asha configuration to find the engine.

components.summary: Process routing, capability matching and dependency plans, with the capability-broker and process-router agents.
components.reason: The agents call `asha capabilities match` and `asha process route`; the broker reads the registry and harness contract from an Asha checkout.

components.summary: The asha-find-skills skill: import an approved candidate into the Asha skill store and mount it through the installer.
components.reason: Import writes $ASHA_HOME/skills and its lock; mounting is the Asha installer's job.
Reads Memory v2 publications and ~/.asha/learnings as primary sources.
Needs the dual opt-in in ~/.asha/config.json and the repository, Asha's live policy guard, and a Workflow-capable harness.

components.summary: Control sessions and Rooms, Memory v2 publication and recovery, and the wrapper-scoped persona.
components.reason: They are the Asha runtime: the dispatcher, Control database, Memory v2 tools and identity merge.
